clue.text: How this order to reassemble the ranks is given

definitions.text: How this order to reassemble the ranks is given

parts.words: How this order to reassemble the ranks is given
parts.note: the command to regroup troops is shouted across the parade ground, so the clue asks the manner of its delivery: by word of mouth

explanation.surface: A drill sergeant's command to regroup the troops, and the manner in which it is delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue asks how such a command is delivered; a bonus is that the word for regrouping troops sits inside the answer after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken command is delivered by mouth, not in writing.

clue.text: Refuse to admit French here — from an authoritative source

indicators.note: to admit means letting the second piece in, inside the word for refuse

parts.note: offal is refuse, rubbish
ici is French for here

explanation.surface: Rejecting the French language here, says someone in authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb but is the noun, rubbish: OFFAL holds ICI.
explanation.definitionFit: Official means authorised, issued by those in authority.

clue.text: Rail components in oriental transport company

indicators.note: components treats the letters of rail as parts to be assembled differently

parts.note: taken as written
oriental means eastern, E

explanation.surface: Railway parts used by an Asian haulage firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'components' rearranges RAIL into AIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: An airline is a business carrying passengers and freight by plane.

clue.text: Roughly an allergy of the voice chamber

indicators.note: roughly signals the letters of an allergy are shuffled into a rough new order

explanation.surface: Something like an allergic reaction affecting the throat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' rearranges AN ALLERGY.
explanation.definitionFit: Laryngeal relates to the larynx, the organ in the throat where sound is produced.

clue.text: Order dessert

definitions.meaning: neatness or tidiness, as in the phrase for things laid out perfectly
a sweet course, here a baked fruit pastry

explanation.surface: A two-word instruction to the waiter: bring the pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple-pie order is perfect neatness, so the hyphenated phrase stands for order; it is also a baked fruit pudding.

clue.text: Supporters of road transport

parts.note: the air-filled rubber rings on which cars and lorries ride, supporting them in a literal sense

explanation.surface: Sounds like a lobby group backing cars and lorries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporters' suggests advocates, but means what physically bears a vehicle's weight on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflated wheels carry the weight of motor vehicles.

clue.text: Seven years labour for monogamy, seven more for bigamy he demanded

definitions.text: Seven years labour for monogamy, seven more for bigamy he demanded

parts.words: Seven years labour for monogamy, seven more for bigamy he demanded
parts.note: in Genesis, Jacob's father-in-law made him work seven years for Leah and seven more for Rachel

explanation.surface: A harsh father-in-law sets the price of one wife and then of two.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible story: Jacob served seven years for Rachel, was given her sister Leah instead, then served seven more for Rachel.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis this man is the father of Leah and Rachel who extracted fourteen years of service from Jacob.

clue.text: Roundhead in a sorry plight gets the point

indicators.note: in places the head of round inside the word for a sorry plight

parts.note: a pickle is a sorry plight, a mess
the head, or first letter, of round is R

explanation.surface: A Civil War Parliamentarian in trouble finally understands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roundhead' suggests Cromwell's side in the English Civil War, but it means the first letter of 'round'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prickle is a thorn or spine, a sharp point.

clue.text: What a ring hasn't that The Ring has (at long last)

definitions.text: What a ring hasn't that The Ring has (at long last)

parts.words: What a ring hasn't that The Ring has (at long last)
parts.note: a circle has no termination, while Wagner's very long opera cycle does finally reach its close

explanation.surface: A riddle contrasting a circle with Wagner's operas.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ring is Wagner's four-opera cycle, some fifteen hours long, hence 'at long last'.
explanation.definitionFit: A conclusion is the final part, which a circle lacks.

clue.text: Government dispensing

definitions.meaning: the body running a country, the executive of the day
giving out, as medicine or justice is handed out

explanation.surface: A state handing things out.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the executive in power and the act of giving out medicine or justice.

clue.text: Novel place for a festival

parts.note: a fictional town that hosts a festival in a 1951 comic novel by J. B. Priestley

explanation.surface: Looks like a call for an original venue to hold a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' seems to mean new or original, but it means 'from a novel': J. B. Priestley's Festival at Farbridge, set in an invented English town.
explanation.definitionFit: Priestley invented the town as the setting for the festival in his novel's title.

clue.text: Such a date one has not foreseen

definitions.text: Such a date one has not foreseen

parts.words: Such a date one has not foreseen
parts.note: a romantic meeting arranged with a stranger you have never set eyes on, read as a date you have literally not seen beforehand

explanation.surface: A date that comes as a surprise, an appointment nobody predicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreseen' suggests predicting the future, but here it means seen before: the partner on such a date is someone you have never laid eyes on.
explanation.definitionFit: A date with a stranger is named for not having seen them, as one lacking sight cannot see.

clue.text: A drink in China, with It, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of the two words may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Ordering a drink in China, together with something trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges CHINA and IT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany, a beverage.

clue.text: Dwarf is a chap with a singularly small family

parts.note: a chap is a man
singularly suggests one alone, the Roman numeral I
kin is one's family or relations, a small group by blood

explanation.surface: A small person described as a fellow with a tiny family.
explanation.walkthrough: The '-kin' ending is also a diminutive suffix, fitting 'small'.
explanation.definitionFit: A manikin is a little man, a pygmy or homunculus.

clue.text: Bare terrain including a ridge

indicators.note: including says the letters sit inside the words bare terrain, straddling the gap

explanation.surface: A description of mountain country: bleak ground with a ridge running across it.
explanation.walkthrough: The run lies across 'bARE TErrain'.
explanation.definitionFit: An arete is a sharp mountain crest between two glacial valleys.

clue.text: Silly nit, less polite when he's not invited

indicators.note: silly signals the letters of nit are muddled into a new order

parts.note: less polite is ruder

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at a gatecrasher: a foolish, rude person who turns up uninvited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' turns NIT into INT.
explanation.definitionFit: An unwelcome person who forces their way in is a trespasser, one not asked to come.

clue.text: Aristocratic sly thing is uncommonly ugly

parts.note: U means upper-class, aristocratic

indicators.note: uncommonly signals the letters of sly thing are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A sneaky upper-class creature that is remarkably hideous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncommonly' rearranges SLY THING. U for upper-class comes from 1950s British talk of 'U and non-U' speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsightly means unpleasant to look at.

clue.text: Puts playgoers and racehorses in their places

definitions.text: Puts playgoers and racehorses in their places

parts.words: Puts playgoers and racehorses in their places
parts.note: theatre-goers sit in the stalls, the front seats downstairs, and racehorses start from stalls; placing either there settles them

explanation.surface: An usher and a racecourse handler both directing others to their spots.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, IN STALLS: the stalls are the ground-floor seats in a British theatre and the starting gates at a horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something in position is to set it in place.

clue.text: Breaking down when City girl returns

indicators.note: returns says the whole run of city and girl is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
Lana is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone collapses emotionally when a woman comes back from the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns CITY plus LANA as one string, giving ANAL then YTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Analytic describes splitting something into its parts for study, the process of breaking it down.

clue.text: Most orderly and cosy home in which to feed

indicators.note: in which says the second piece goes inside the cosy home

parts.note: a nest is a cosy home
to feed is to eat

explanation.surface: A neat, snug house where meals are taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cosy home' is a bird's nest; 'in which' places the word for feeding inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatest is the superlative of tidy, the most orderly.

clue.text: She has sex-appeal in daylight

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: daylight comes from the sun
SA is the abbreviation for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A woman who looks attractive in broad day.
explanation.walkthrough: SA is the crossword abbreviation for sex appeal; 'She' is the definition, a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, so the pronoun stands for her.

clue.text: Bad-tasting, these French wells

parts.note: bad-tasting can mean sour
ces is French for these

explanation.surface: A complaint that these French springs taste foul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wells' reads as springs in the surface and is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sources are springs where water rises, like wells.

clue.text: In a predicament, fiddle

definitions.meaning: to play the violin badly, scraping the bow

explanation.surface: Someone in trouble plays the violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a' is the link: one is said to be 'in a scrape'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a tight spot one gets into and the act of drawing a bow harshly across strings.

clue.text: Making an excellent comeback after many extol her

indicators.note: after puts the reversed piece behind the words for many and extol

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
to extol is to laud or praise

indicators.note: comeback means the piece for an excellent is turned round

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written AI

explanation.surface: A woman returns triumphantly once crowds have sung her praises.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, read as letters AI, is reversed by 'comeback' to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, so the pronoun stands for her.

clue.text: Current inclusion of gold one found in order

indicators.note: inclusion of means the pieces for gold and one are put inside the current

parts.note: DC is direct current
or is gold in heraldry
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Gold found while digging into a modern trend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' means a style of classical column, not a command.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is one of the classical orders of architecture.

clue.text: Food for a gentile returning 'injured

indicators.note: returning makes the word for a gentile run backwards

parts.note: goy is a Yiddish word for a non-Jew
injured means hurt

explanation.surface: Something to eat for a non-Jew coming back wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns GOY into YOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoghurt is a fermented milk product eaten as a food.

clue.text: Ruler of less than half America, Good Queen Bess

indicators.note: less than half picks the opening three of the seven letters of America

parts.note: Elizabeth I, known as Good Queen Bess, is ER (Elizabeth Regina)

explanation.surface: A monarch governing part of the New World: Elizabeth I.
explanation.walkthrough: AME is three letters of AMERICA's seven, less than half.
explanation.definitionFit: An ameer (emir) is a Muslim prince or governor.

clue.text: Clad in tie ? That's unusual, just the same

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of clad in tie are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that seeing a person dressed in a necktie is strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges CLAD IN TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical means exactly alike, the same in every detail.

clue.text: Tempting 27's heart with gin perhaps

indicators.note: heart means only the central letters of the answer to 27 across are kept, its ends dropped

parts.note: refers to the answer to 27 across

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters of gin are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something alluring in the core of the previous answer, combined with a spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' keeps ENTIC, the middle five of the nine letters of 27; 'perhaps' turns GIN into ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Enticing means alluring, drawing someone on with temptation.

clue.text: So sky-high go the Shepherd kings, apparently backwards

indicators.note: backwards says the run of letters found in so sky-high is read in reverse
apparently signals the letters are plainly visible in the words so sky-high, across the joins

explanation.surface: Ancient rulers soaring up into the heavens, seemingly in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits backwards across 'SO SKY-High'. The Hyksos were foreign rulers of ancient Egypt, their name long translated as 'shepherd kings'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyksos is the Egyptian dynasty traditionally rendered as rulers of shepherds.
